newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline sees charge.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline sees charge.

text.p: Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline Partners LP and its general partner Santa Fe Pacific Pipelines Inc said they would record a $6 million charge in the quarter ending March 31, related to litigation settlement.
Santa Fe said an agreement was executed with the bankruptcy trustee of El Paso Refinery LP which settled El Paso's claims in civil litigation it filed against Santa Fe.
Under terms of the deal, Santa Fe said it agreed to pay $16 million to El Paso in two equal installments.

The litigation, filed by EPR and El Paso Refining Inc in August 1992, sought damages resulting from promises Santa Fe allegedly made regarding the expansion of its pipelines between El Paso, Texas and Phoenix, Arizona, it said.

Irvin Toole Jr, Chairman of the general partner said: "This settlement, when approved by final, non-appealable court orders, will resolve the civil litigation which the Partnership has faced since 1992."
He said the company would record a charge because the settlement amount exceeded reserves which had been set aside.
The agreement was contingent on certain factors, the company said.
